evidence.question: local-or-systemic
evidence.basis: Swept all 56 .py files under tests/ (43 test modules, tests/conftest.py, 12 fixture modules) by AST parse plus suite-wide regex; 738 def test_ functions counted statically. Exactly ONE new genuine cannot-fail instance found, in a SECOND file (tests/test_docket_reassembly.py:360-362), and no recurrence of the shape anywhere else in 738 tests. Zero assert-True literals (AST Constant-assert scan: no hits), zero empty parametrize lists (literal or name-resolved), zero empty-literal loops, zero comm uses, zero X==X.copy() forms outside the U8.25 comment that documents the removed one. All 6 always-skip candidates were measured OPEN in this environment, so none of them actually skips. The class is therefore a rare, localized defect, not a suite-wide pattern: LOCAL. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: a DIFFERENT class IS systemic and broad - 75 pytest.raises blocks carry neither match= nor any assertion on the caught exception (23 of them in tests with no assertion at all). Those CAN fail (absence or wrong type), so they are NOT cannot-fail; they are blind only to WHICH diagnostic fired. That weakness is systemic, the cannot-fail class is not.

sweep_coverage.method: static+reading (AST parse + regex of all 56; body-level reads of 14)

evidence.verification_standard: Mutations only under state/verify/U8.30/; IMPORTED_FROM verified before any claim (read_manifest=src/resextract/docket/manifest.py, _block=tests/test_docket_reassembly.py). No whole-suite run; no test file was run at all - the demonstration used the real module objects directly.

scanner_artifacts_disclosed.note: my first-pass detector flagged the legitimate post-block-assert pattern; and a literal-assert regex over-matched quoted strings, producing a list of ~400 normal asserts with no assert-True among them - the AST Constant-assert scan is authoritative and found ZERO. These are my own detector artifacts, NOT findings.

candidates.demonstration: Both sides are the same call on the same file; _block = json.dumps([row.model_dump() for row in m.material], sort_keys=True). Demonstrated, not argued: I imported the real test module and the real read_manifest (IMPORTED_FROM verified), then evaluated the predicate AS WRITTEN on a known-good manifest and on a schema-valid LIE. AS WRITTEN returned True for BOTH. The value-vs-measurement form of the same check (_block(read_manifest(path)) == EXPECTED where EXPECTED is a measurement of the known-good artifact) returned True for the good file and False for the lie. So the assertion cannot observe a perturbation that an independent expectation does observe. Also matches the two-derived-values shape (same source read twice).

NOT relitigated, and now correctly REMOVED: the comment at lines 96-100 states U8.25 removed the 13-file exemption because it protected nothing, and the suite-wide scan for set(frozenset(X)) forms returns only that comment, no live code. Recorded as a fixed prior instance, not a current finding.

candidates.quote: if not before.exists(): pytest.skip('U8.15 pre-repair copy absent')
candidates.demonstration: Measured: state/logs/U8.15/repairs/U0.22.before.json EXISTS (and state/logs/U8.15 exists), so the skip branch is NOT taken in this environment. The guarded test does run.

candidates.quote: pytest.skip('no bindable non-loopback IPv4 address on this host')
candidates.demonstration: Measured by replaying the test's own probe: socket(AF_INET,SOCK_DGRAM).connect(('192.168.2.1',9)) yields 192.168.2.187, non-loopback, so the function returns before reaching the skip. socket.getaddrinfo alone returns no non-loopback address, which is why this looked like an always-skip; the routing-table branch is the one that fires.
Measured: state/kg/duval/graphify-out/graph.json exists=True, so the skipif condition is False and the test runs.

candidates.quote: if _GENUINE_GRAPH.is_file():  # guards the assert at :1611 and the :1619-1621 assertions
candidates.demonstration: Measured: the file exists, so this conditional escape is OPEN and the guarded assertions at :1611 and :1619-1621 do execute. A conditional escape only blinds if its guard is always false here; this one is always true.

candidates.quote: pytest.skip('git is not available on PATH; cannot test ignore semantics')
candidates.demonstration: Measured: shutil.which('git') = /usr/bin/git, and pathlib.Path('.git').exists() is True (we are in a git work tree), so neither the :96 nor the :99 skip fires.

candidates.quote: skip = pytest.mark.skip(reason=LIVE_SKIP_REASON)  # applied to @pytest.mark.live items unless --live or RESEXTRACT_LIVE=1
candidates.demonstration: Genuinely always-skip in a default run, but INTENTIONAL and correctly built: it is opt-in via --live or RESEXTRACT_LIVE=1, it is applied only to explicitly marked live items, and pytest_terminal_summary (:70-80) exists specifically to make skipped live tests loud so that 'N skipped' is never read as 'N passed'. By design, so not a defect.

Confirmed as type-only, and truthfully NOT cannot-fail: the block raises if no exception or the wrong type occurs, so it can fail. What it cannot do is distinguish WHICH IntegrityError fired, because there is no match= and no assertion on the caught exception anywhere in the test. This is the systemic weakness class: 75 such blocks of 93 raises-with across the suite, 23 of them inside tests with no assertion at all. Representative peers: test_store_v2.py:516/518/522/524/528/530/534/537, test_store_v3.py:218, test_writer_detection.py:299, test_git_source.py:156/160/207/209/227/229/239/244, test_occamy_client.py:410/452/486.

The broadest member of the type-only set: pytest.raises(Exception) with no match= and no assertion anywhere in the test (test_manifest_forbids_unknown_fields). It can fail if nothing is raised, but it accepts ANY exception - arguably the strongest single case for tightening, since a wrong error type is indistinguishable from the intended one. Peers of the same breadth: tests/test_docket_provenance.py:378, :651, :885.

My own scanner's false positive: the body contains no assert because it delegates to _assert_guard_b (test_kg_ingest.py:72), which carries 12 real asserts (:75-84) including three with explicit failure messages. The same holds for :309 -> _assert_guard_a (:62, 4 asserts at :65-69) and :321 -> _assert_guard_b. Assertion-bearing support code, correctly factored.

Looks like a no-assert test but is not blind: it asserts ACCEPTANCE by requiring that no exception is raised, and it is parametrized over the real vocabulary (store.VERDICT_VOCAB, len=4, measured). The negative twin at :88 catches rejection. Same shape at :107 LANE_TYPES len=5, :120 LANE_STATUSES len=5, :133 EVIDENCE_SOURCE_KINDS len=2 - all non-empty, so not vacuous parametrisation either.

candidates.quote: try: M.DocketManifest.model_validate({**u55, 'resultz': []}) except M.ValidationError: pass else: raise AssertionError('extra=forbid no longer refuses a misspelled key')
candidates.demonstration: My scanner flagged it because the handler body is only Pass, but this is the CORRECT idiom: the else-clause raises AssertionError when validation wrongly SUCCEEDS, so the test fails if extra=forbid regresses. Fully failable. Same at :1179-1186 and :1429-1434. The other 5 except-pass sites are environment-probe or cleanup fallbacks, read and confirmed: test_cli.py:786/790 (candidate-IP probes with a fallback list), test_dashboard_auth.py:255/268 (probe chain before the same skip discussed above), test_git_source.py:173 (os.fspath on non-path file objects inside an open() spy).

U N V E R I F I E D. This was a spot-check for the WS.29-style spurious class (a tuple compared to a list, or an unsorted comm). Suite-wide there is no comm use at all (0 occurrences) and no set-vs-list comparison: test_cli.py:367 compares set(cli.IMPLEMENTED) to IMPLEMENTED_SUBCOMMANDS, which is a set LITERAL at test_cli.py:354, so it is set-vs-set and sound. For this line I could not resolve LINE_BUFFER_PREFIX's type - it is not defined at module level in that file - so I cannot demonstrate either way. No mismatch is evidenced; recording it as unverified rather than accusing it.

next_unit_hint: If the suite is to be tightened, the highest-value and lowest-risk target is the SYSTEMIC type-only class, not the single cannot-fail: add match= (or an assert on excinfo.value) to tests/test_docket_assemble.py:518 and tests/test_docket_provenance.py:378/651/885, which use pytest.raises(Exception) and would accept ANY exception as the right answer. Separately, tests/test_docket_reassembly.py:360-362 should be replaced by a comparison against a recorded expectation (the _block of a known-good artifact) rather than a second read of the same file; the demonstration file state/verify/U8.30/m_lie.json is the ready-made perturbation to prove the replacement is not blind. Assertions to leave alone: the three else-raise AssertionError try-blocks in test_docket_reassembly.py, the _assert_guard_a/_assert_guard_b helpers, and the 'accepts_vocabulary' parametrized tests - all were checked and all can fail.
